description: Indulge in the iconic flavors of Butter Chicken, a beloved Indian classic known as Murgh Makhani. This rich and creamy dish features tender chicken pieces simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy, subtly spiced and finished with butter and cream. It is the ultimate comfort food, perfect for a special meal or a cozy dinner.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Sear until lightly browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add 1 tablespoon of butter. Once melted, add the finely chopped onion and sauté over medium heat until translucent and softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.

instructions.title: Add Tomatoes and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, remaining 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, and 1/2 teaspoon garam masala. Mix well and bring the mixture to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes, or until the oil begins to separate from the tomato mixture and it thickens.

instructions.title: Simmer with Cashews and Blend
instructions.text: Drain the soaked cashews and add them to the tomato mixture along with 1/2 cup of water. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook for 5 minutes to soften the cashews further. Remove from heat and let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. You may need to do this in batches. For an extra smooth gravy, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish the Dish
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan. Add the cooked chicken pieces, crushed Kasoori Methi, and sugar (if using). Stir well and simmer gently for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter. Heat gently for 2-3 minutes, ensuring it does not boil vigorously after adding the cream. Check for seasoning and adjust salt or sugar if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.

tips: Marinating the chicken for a longer period (up to 4 hours) will yield more tender and flavorful results, allowing the spices to deeply penetrate the meat.
For an incredibly silky-smooth gravy, after blending the tomato and cashew mixture, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve before returning it to the pan. This removes any small bits of onion or cashew.
Kasoori Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) is a signature ingredient for Butter Chicken and provides a unique aroma and depth of flavor. Do not omit it for an authentic taste.
Always add the heavy cream and the final knob of butter at the very end of cooking, and heat gently without boiling to prevent the cream from curdling and to maintain its luscious texture.
Adjust the amount of red chili powder for your desired level of heat. For a richer color without too much spice, a pinch of Kashmiri red chili powder can be used.
article:
Unlock the Secrets of Classic Murgh Makhani: Your Guide to Authentic Butter Chicken

Few dishes evoke the same universal comfort and culinary delight as Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian creation, famed for its rich, creamy tomato gravy and succulent pieces of chicken, has captivated palates worldwide. Whether you’re a seasoned chef or a home cook eager to explore the vibrant world of Indian cuisine, mastering this classic is a rewarding journey. Prepare to transform your kitchen into an aromatic haven as we dive deep into the art of crafting the perfect Butter Chicken.

## What is Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani?

At its heart, Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, translates simply to "chicken with butter." This beloved dish originated in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, a happy accident born from combining leftover tandoori chicken with a rich tomato and butter gravy. The result was a culinary masterpiece that quickly gained international fame.

Classic Murgh Makhani is characterized by its velvety smooth, slightly sweet, and tangy tomato-based sauce, generously enriched with butter and cream. The chicken, traditionally marinated in yogurt and spices and then cooked in a tandoor (or grilled/pan-fried), remains incredibly tender, soaking up the luxurious flavors of the gravy. Key spices like garam masala, turmeric, cumin, and the aromatic kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) contribute to its distinctive taste profile, creating a symphony of flavors that is both complex and incredibly comforting. It’s a dish that balances richness with a delicate acidity, making it universally appealing and incredibly satisfying.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key components. Don't be intimidated by the list; each ingredient plays a crucial role in building the dish's signature flavor.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   1 kg boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1 cup plain yogurt
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   Salt to taste

**For the Makhani (Butter Chicken) Gravy:**
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   2 large onions, finely chopped
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (800g) can crushed tomatoes or 6-7 medium fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes (optional, for extra creaminess)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1 teaspoon coriander powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or more, to taste)
*   1-2 tablespoons sugar (or honey/maple syrup), to balance acidity
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create a show-stopping Butter Chicken that will impress even the most discerning palates.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Preheat your oven broiler, grill, or a large skillet over medium-high heat. If broiling, arrange chicken on a baking sheet and cook for 10-15 minutes, flipping once, until lightly charred and cooked through. If grilling, cook until done with nice grill marks. If pan-frying, add a tablespoon of oil to the skillet and cook chicken in batches until browned and cooked through. Set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter with the oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes (or fresh tomato puree), red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, and garam masala. Mix well and bring to a simmer. If using soaked cashews, add them now.
5.  **Simmer and Blend:** Reduce heat to low, cover, and let the gravy simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down. Remove from heat and let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the gravy to a blender (or use an immersion blender) and blend until perfectly smooth. This step is crucial for the velvety texture of Butter Chicken. Pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot for an even silkier consistency.
6.  **Finish the Gravy:** Return the pot to low heat. Stir in the kasoori methi, heavy cream, sugar, and salt to taste. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, ensuring the gravy doesn't boil vigorously after adding cream.
7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy. Stir to coat the chicken thoroughly and heat through for another 5-10 minutes. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tricks:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Smoke Factor:** Traditionally, tandoori chicken lends a smoky depth. If you don't have a tandoor, you can replicate this by cooking the chicken under a broiler until slightly charred, or even by placing a small piece of hot charcoal in a bowl within the pot and covering it for a few minutes to infuse a smoky aroma into the finished dish.
*   **Smoothness is Supreme:** Blending the gravy until absolutely smooth is non-negotiable for that signature creamy texture. A high-speed blender followed by sieving will give you the best results.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust! The beauty of Murgh Makhani lies in the balance of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy. Add more sugar if too tart, more salt as needed, and a pinch more chili if you prefer a spicier kick.
*   **Kasoori Methi Magic:** Don't skip the kasoori methi. Lightly crush the dried fenugreek leaves between your palms before adding them; this releases their essential oils and distinctive, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor that is vital for authentic Butter Chicken.
*   **Good Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality butter, fresh cream, and ripe, flavorful tomatoes for the best possible taste.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments.

*   **Bread:** Warm, fluffy Naan bread (garlic naan is a favorite!) or soft Roti are perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy.
*   **Rice:** Steamed Basmati rice is an excellent choice, providing a neutral canvas for the vibrant flavors of the chicken. A simple jeera rice (cumin rice) also pairs beautifully.
*   **Sides:** A fresh cucumber and onion salad, or a cooling raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and spices), can provide a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Beverages:** A mango lassi (yogurt drink) is a classic pairing, offering a sweet and creamy balance.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, you can adapt it to suit different preferences and dietary needs.

*   **Vegetarian Alternatives:** For a delicious meat-free option, substitute the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), firm tofu, or even chickpeas. The cooking process for the gravy remains the same. This is often called Paneer Butter Masala.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your liking. For a milder dish, use less; for more heat, add a bit more or a finely chopped green chili.
*   **Dairy-Free:** To make it dairy-free, replace butter with a plant-based butter alternative and heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or a cashew cream (blended soaked cashews with water).
*   **Healthier Options:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or use a low-fat cream alternative. You can also bake or grill the chicken without oil.
*   **Tomato Base:** While canned crushed tomatoes are convenient, using fresh, ripe tomatoes, blanched, peeled, and pureed, will offer a slightly fresher flavor profile.

Embark on this culinary adventure and discover the joy of making authentic Butter Chicken in your own kitchen. Its irresistible aroma, luxurious texture, and unforgettable taste will undoubtedly make it a regular favorite in your home. Enjoy the journey to creating this timeless Indian classic!
